chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Wassaq, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from the one he mentioned, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who dies while he has a debt from the month of Ramadan. Who will pay it off on his behalf? He said: The people most entitled to do so. I said: And if the person most entitled to do so is a woman? He said: No, only men.
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying the debts of a deceased man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hierarchy of heirs responsible for settling a deceased man's debts, specifically excluding women from this financial obligation in favor of male relatives. This ruling reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential view that while women inherit, the primary duty of debt repayment falls upon male heirs who are typically the financial providers, distinguishing it from general inheritance distribution.
